kurz: Honey keeps gingerbread soft, and special [[triebmittel|raising agents]] lighten the heavy dough: baker's ammonia and potash.
bild_im_kopf: Like a kitchen sponge cloth: honey draws in moisture and won't let go of it.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Warm honey and sugar, add spices, leave to cool
schluesselmomente.warum: Warm, everything dissolves easily and the spices release their aroma into the honey.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Work in flour and dissolved baker's ammonia or potash
schluesselmomente.warum: Yeast could hardly cope with so much honey and sugar. These raising salts only release gas in the oven.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Rest the dough at least overnight, traditionally longer
schluesselmomente.warum: The flour fully absorbs the moisture and the flavours come together.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Bake, then store airtight, with an apple slice if needed
schluesselmomente.warum: Honey draws in moisture. In the tin it stays in the gingerbread, which even gets softer over the days.
